questions.prompt: What should an unfamiliar agent see first?
questions.context: Both approaches still provide the full API reference. This chooses the starting point. These cards are illustrative documentation layouts.
questions.recommendation: Start with tasks. An agent can choose a path before loading the relevant details.

preview.html:
What do you want to do?

  • Run a prepared interface
  • Create a one-off interface
  • Build a reusable skill interface
  • Look up a command or API

Fungi reference

  • CLI: open · collect · reopen
  • Page API: ready · submit · cancel
  • Delivery modes and result format
  • Optional drafts, attachments and limits

questions.prompt: How much documentation should an installed copy include offline?
questions.context: This concerns Fungi-specific documentation, not copies of third-party framework manuals. The development wiki and test evidence do not need to ship.
questions.recommendation: Include the complete Fungi reference and a few small working examples. An agent should be able to use or author an interface without finding the source checkout.

options.label: Complete Fungi reference + small working examples (recommended)
Core reference offline; tutorials and examples mainly online

questions.prompt: What should the main examples teach?
questions.context: This chooses example depth. It does not add a new component library or authorize a grill-form port.
questions.recommendation: Use a few small, complete flows: a plain response, an image/canvas result, and a reusable skill interface. Show the input, launch, completion and returned data together.

options.label: Mostly short snippets for individual APIs
One rich workflow explained in depth, such as grill-form

questions.prompt: What feels missing or unnecessary in this outline?
questions.context: Use Notes, or Comment on preview to mark a section. The structure is a proposal. A consuming skill keeps its own methodology and short launch/response recipe; Fungi supplies reference documentation.
questions.recommendation: Keep this small and expand when a real workflow needs more explanation.

answers.question: What should an unfamiliar agent see first?
answers.notes: i'm just concerned that the task-oriented way will stunt or constrain an agent's own creativity. we will have much more consistent results, sure, but some agents might blindly follow or even take it as a rule of law or strict instruction. i like the consistency but i also like to allow freedom of thought (creativity). anyway just me rambling, tell me what you think and push back if you need to.

answers.question: How much documentation should an installed copy include offline?
answers.choice: Complete Fungi reference + small working examples (recommended)

answers.question: What should the main examples teach?
What feels missing or unnecessary in this outline?
answers.notes: yep keep it simple and concise. don't bloat it.
